help_encryption_desc: All text is encrypted on your device using AES-256-GCM (authenticated encryption). Your password is strengthened with Argon2id (128MB memory, 4 iterations) before generating the encryption key. The output is Base64-encoded. No data ever leaves your device (no internet permission).
help_boxes_desc: Each box has its own independent password. Messages are encrypted at rest in a database protected by SQLCipher. You decrypt each message on-demand inside the chat. Box passwords are never stored on disk except in Permanent mode (see Lock Modes).
help_lock_modes_desc: Control how often you must enter the box password:
help_lock_always: Ask password every time you open the box.
help_lock_timed: Remember password for a set time during this session (cleared on minimize).
help_lock_session: Remember password for this session only (cleared on minimize).
help_lock_permanent: Remember password across restarts. Password is stored encrypted in the device Keystore. Only available if you accept the security risk.
help_app_lock_desc: The app PIN is hashed with Argon2id (64MB memory) and stored in EncryptedSharedPreferences. It supports letters, numbers, and symbols (4 to 32 characters). 5 wrong attempts trigger a 30-second lockout. Fingerprint uses Android BiometricPrompt. Without a PIN, anyone who opens the app has full access.
help_backup_desc: Setting a PIN protects your data. If the app has a problem, you can recover all your data by entering your PIN. Without a PIN, data may be lost if something goes wrong.
help_auto_lock_desc: Controls how long the app stays unlocked after being minimized. Immediate: locks as soon as you leave the app. 30s-30min: you can return without re-entering PIN if the time hasn't expired. Only works if an app PIN is set.
help_screenshot_desc: Prevents screenshots and screen recording using FLAG_SECURE. Disable this if you need to capture the screen (e.g., for documentation), but be aware that sensitive data may be visible.
help_security_desc:
• CryptoSafe has NO internet permission — your data never leaves the device.
• Without an app PIN, anyone with your phone can access all data.
• 'Permanent' box mode stores the password encrypted in Keystore — it survives app restarts.
• 'Session' and 'Timed' passwords are RAM-only and lost on minimize.
• The database is encrypted with SQLCipher using a random 32-byte key stored in Keystore.
• Box passwords are never logged or transmitted.
help_risks_title: What CryptoSafe Does NOT Protect Against
help_risks_desc:
• Keyloggers or screen recorders on a compromised device.
• Physical theft of your unlocked phone.
• You sharing your passwords with others.
• Weak box passwords (use the generator for strong ones).
help_share_desc: From any app (WhatsApp, Telegram, browser), tap Share and select CryptoSafe. You can encrypt the text, decrypt it, or save it to a box. Text saved to a box is stored as-is without additional encryption by the box password.
help_autodelete_desc: Each box has an auto-delete setting. Messages older than the set time are automatically deleted on open. Options: 1 hour, 6 hours, 12 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or never.
help_changepw_desc: Changing a box password re-encrypts all messages one by one. Messages that fail to decrypt or are pre-encrypted (shared from other apps) are skipped and remain unchanged.
help_quantum_desc:
According to NIST IR 8105 (Report on Post-Quantum Cryptography), symmetric algorithms with 256-bit keys such as AES-256 remain resistant to quantum attack: Grover's algorithm only halves their effective strength to 128 bits, which is still beyond practical attack. NIST's quantum-vulnerable list targets RSA and ECC (asymmetric) keys via Shor's algorithm; CryptoSafe uses only symmetric cryptography (AES-256-GCM + Argon2id) and stores no RSA/ECC keys, so it is not affected by the primary quantum threat.
According to NIST SP 800-63B and the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet, password strength — not the algorithm — is the weakest link. Use a long, random, unique password (NIST: length matters more than complexity). The app includes a built-in strong password generator — always use it.
